title: Bodywork, Occupant Packaging and Refinishing
author: Erudior
description: Compare panel joints, glazing, closures, lamps and restraint layouts. Form and fit an original panel and validate occupant controls, access and visibility. Includes a parts atlas and an assessed modification workshop.
changelog: Added an individual parts atlas, hands-on modification workshop, instance-level build ledger and pre/post verification.

lessons.title: Lay out the car around the driver
lessons.body:
Entry skills: complete Chassis Design, Welding and Fabrication, Cooling, Cabin HVAC and Refrigerant Practice, or demonstrate the equivalent workshop skills.

Begin with a real seat, pedal location and steering wheel in a stable full-size mock-up. Record hip reference, eye location, sightlines, reach, ingress and pedal travel. Allow for shoes, trim, steering travel and adjustment. Reserve locations for restraint anchors and side structure for engineering review. Select obtainable safety glazing and its mounting envelope early.

## Worked shop case

A driver fits when seated, but a fixed steering wheel blocks entry once a roof rail is mocked up. The failure concerns the path into the seat. Include the opening and travel envelope in the next revision.

## Guided practice

A driver mock-up provides 64 mm static clearance where the design target for that mock-up is 75 mm. Give the shortfall in mm.

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

**What you will produce.** A learner-formed panel, physical fit check, finishing coupon or documented professional finish, and as-built body drawing.

Identify individual components in the parts atlas and trace their interfaces on your exact donor drawing.

lessons.title: Doors, closures, glass, weather sealing and visibility
topics: Doors, closures, glass, weather sealing and visibility
lessons.body:
A closure combines hinges, latch, striker, seals, stops and reinforcement. The hinges carry its weight; the latch must engage securely without having to lift a sagging closure into position. Weatherstrips seal compressed interfaces; water passing the outer beltline of a door needs managed drainage. Compare welded or bonded fixed panels with service-removable panels and record replacement access. A serviceable opening also needs trim clearance, inside release, glass guides and water management.

Laminated glass retains fragments in an interlayer when broken. Tempered glass fractures differently. Windshields and other glazing positions require the appropriate approved glazing for the vehicle and jurisdiction; side glass can also be laminated. Bonded windshields may contribute to body and restraint performance and can carry camera optics. Wiper sweep, washer delivery, defrost airflow and mirrors or cameras determine usable visibility. Verify part markings, aperture geometry, retention method, cure and calibration with approved information.

## Worked shop case

A mock-up door shuts smoothly with its glass down but binds with the glass raised. Check hinge alignment, glass guides, roof seal compression and frame deflection before moving the striker. Moving the striker first can disguise a glass alignment problem and change latch engagement.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: After a trim change, the inside carpet is wet below a door that passes the exterior seal check. Where do you look?
step: Trace water entering the outer glass slot.
step: Verify membrane sealing and drain paths.
answer: Water may be correctly entering the door cavity and then escaping through a failed inner barrier or blocked drain.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Fit a removable practice closure or panel. Record gaps and flushness at identified points, latch or fastener engagement, two egress observations, and water path. Log glazing, wiper and demist choices for the full build.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Lighting optics, seats, restraints and occupant controls
topics: Lighting optics, seats, restraints and occupant controls
lessons.body:
Halogen lamps use a heated filament, HID units use an arc and ballast, and LED units use semiconductor emitters, drivers and thermal management. Beam shape depends on the light source, optics, aim and installation. A physically compatible bulb socket does not establish that a different source works in that optic or is lawful. Compare the complete appropriate lamp assembly, photometric approval or marking requirements, mounting height, aim, compatibility and service access for the intended use.

A seat, track, anchor, belt, head restraint and any airbags work together. Belt geometry changes with the occupant and seat travel. Compare seat-integrated versus body-mounted belt load paths and verify compatible anchor support using reviewed design information. Do not mix restraint elements on appearance. Consider pedal travel, positive throttle return, steering reach, head clearance and sight lines through the complete adjustment range. Retain a specialist review of restraint and crash-related systems.

## Worked shop case

A donor seat carries its upper belt anchor. Installing it on custom sliders now sends upper-belt loads through the seat and sliders to the floor. A floor designed for a seat with a body-mounted upper anchor may lack a verified path for this load. Resolve it with the designer before drilling or commissioning.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: One candidate headlamp draws less current yet produces glare on a wall. What does current establish?
step: It informs the circuit load.
step: Verify optical compatibility and the prescribed aim and approval for that assembly.
answer: Lower current alone does not establish a usable legal beam.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Mock up a seat and pedals with intended occupants and record reach, visibility, adjustment and emergency exit checks. Identify belt-anchor loads, lamp assemblies and aim method on the as-built drawings. Record independent review of safety-critical choices.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Turn an exterior shape into a buildable panel
lessons.body:
A buck is a physical form defining the panel shape. Plot cross-sections from a common datum and install them at numbered stations. Design panel splits, flange returns, fastener access, edge treatment and water paths before forming. Separate removable skin from load-bearing structures and occupant restraint attachments.

## Worked shop case

A panel is 404 mm outside edge to outside edge across a 410 mm trial opening. If centered on the same axis it leaves a nominal 3 mm gap per side. Fit variability and hinge travel still need inspection.

## Guided practice

A 508 mm opening takes a 500 mm centered panel. Enter nominal gap per side in mm.

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Your design

Use full-size seat and glazing references. Submit a section drawing, buck stations, attachment detail, target gaps and an access test. Identify required lighting or glazing evidence and link the selected finish process to its safety data and shop controls.

```assignment
writing: design
```

## Component design review

Compare the candidates in the component register and bring your selected configuration into this design.

```assignment
writing: component-selection
```

Read a modification card, choose a baseline and identify the changed parts, including hardware and seals.

lessons.title: Form and fit a removable skin
lessons.body:
Transfer the chosen section to a template, establish a datum edge and form a representative panel in a suitable shop. Deburr edges and protect nearby wiring. Trial-fit with temporary location hardware and test removal in the intended order. Keep first articles away from structural or restraint use. Read coating product safety data and discuss process and facility choice before applying final paint.

## Worked shop case

A panel fits before its return flange is formed. After forming, one edge pulls away. Recheck the section template and flange sequence while the mounting datums remain fixed.

## Guided practice

The first gap is 2 mm and the opposite gap 6 mm. Give the difference in mm.

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## US rules at the workbench

For US spray finishing, determine whether EPA's Auto Body Rule (40 CFR Part 63 Subpart HHHHHH) applies to the operation, materials and operator. The personal-vehicle provision has conditions, including a threshold of more than two vehicles or pieces of mobile equipment spray-coated per year, even without compensation. Local air and fire rules can still apply. Covered workplaces also evaluate 29 CFR 1910.107 for flammable/combustible spray finishing, PPE and hazard communication. Obtain component documentation for glazing, lamps and belts. Keep finish safety data and process records.

[EPA — Auto Body Rule, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart HHHHHH](https://www.epa.gov/collision-repair-campaign/about-epas-auto-body-rule) · [40 CFR 63.11169(d)(3) — personal-use conditions](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title40-vol16/pdf/CFR-2025-title40-vol16-part63-subpartHHHHHH.pdf) · [OSHA — spray finishing, 29 CFR 1910.107](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.107) · [OSHA — Hazard Communication, 29 CFR 1910.1200](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.1200) · [NHTSA — equipment standards and a specific kit-manufacturer interpretation](https://www.nhtsa.gov/interpretations/19664ztv)

## Workshop preparation

Use sheet-edge protection, secure work and supervised cutting/forming. Choose a low-hazard coupon process or a qualified paint facility. Isocyanate spraying requires professional exposure controls. Protect electrical equipment during seal tests.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Bring the selected component record to the lab and enter what you personally inspected, made, measured or assembled, with the part identifier and actual conditions.

lessons.title: Size a removable speaker adapter without fouling the glass
topics: Size a removable speaker adapter without fouling the glass
lessons.body:
Open the parts atlas for this system. Trace a parent assembly into its named children and mounting hardware. Explain the function of each item, identify its controlling dimensions or interfaces, then decide which pieces you can machine or fabricate, which you can assemble and which to obtain as qualified assemblies. Put exact drawing or donor references beside your decision.

## Parts on the bench

Exterior, glazing, cabin and access, Interior and exterior detail, Body hardware and interior controls. The quick references linked below include the function, design, fabrication or installation route, and verification of every indexed item.

## Modifications to evaluate

- Sound treatment and door-speaker adapters
- Complete headlamp assembly replacement
- Seat and slider substitution
- Spoiler or front splitter

## Worked example

A door mock-up offers 51 mm depth to the lowered glass measured from the mounting face. A driver extends 58 mm behind its flange. A 12 mm adapter ideally leaves 51 + 12 − 58 = 5 mm clearance before seals compress and the assembly moves. Confirm both rear clearance and front grille clearance physically.

## Guided decision

```example fade=1
problem: A second driver needs 61 mm depth with the same adapter. What static rear margin remains?
step: Subtract driver depth from available depth plus adapter thickness.
answer: 2 mm before tolerances or movement. Compare with measured design allowance and revise if inadequate.
```

## Independent workshop

Make a card or sheet adapter using actual driver and opening templates. Measure the least clearance throughout glass travel, preserve water management and document all fasteners.

Open a modification card for its design, build and test sequence. Record original and changed readings under comparable conditions. Separate physical evidence from predictions and document a safe rollback.

```assignment
writing: modification-record
```

lessons.title: Check latching, sealing and maintenance
lessons.body:
Document panel fit along its perimeter, sound attachment and access after final mounting. On the finished vehicle separately verify door latches, sightlines, mirrors, lights, belt anchors, glazing, wipers and defogging under their applicable criteria. An attractive skin has no implied crash rating. Use a low-pressure water check on a suitable body sample, keeping electrical components protected.

## Worked shop case

A removable panel passes a fit check but prevents replacement of the cabin filter. Rework access now, then repeat both service and seal checks after reassembly.

## Guided practice

At four equally spaced stations gaps are 3, 4, 5 and 4 mm. What is the range in mm?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Practical sign-off

The fitted physical part can be removed and installed with its intended access and has measured gaps against the drawing. Record actual measurements and the disposition of faults. Submit the physical evidence in the workshop record.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Close each build-relevant component row with its measured result, reviewer disposition or an identified open issue and retest. Transfer the accepted configuration to your capstone record.

Reconcile required, issued, installed and verified quantities against the physical assembly and mark unresolved items.

references.title: Component register and build evidence
references.body:
For this course examine Body panel and surface finish; Closures, hinges, latch and seals; Glazing, wiper and washer; Lighting and signaling; Seating, belts and restraints; Pedals and controls. Document manufacturer, part revision, drawing, selection, applicable authority or service requirement, installer, measured result with units, and reviewer disposition. Begin in design and update after installation.

| Family | Candidate designs | What changes | What to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Body panel and surface finish | Stamped / hand-formed / composite; single-stage / basecoat-clearcoat finish | Thermal expansion, joint movement, coating compatibility and exposure determine a finish plan. | Record fit, substrate preparation, coating data, shop controls and coupon outcome. |
| Closures, hinges, latch and seals | Hinged / removable panel; bonded / compressed seal | Load, latch engagement, service access and water path differ. | Measure gap and flushness, evaluate egress and verify drainage. |
| Glazing, wiper and washer | Laminated / tempered; bonded / gasketed glazing; coordinated sweep | Retention, optics and field of view depend on part and position. | Document markings, sweep/washer coverage, demist and calibration evidence. |
| Lighting and signaling | Halogen / HID / LED assemblies | Optic, source, driver and heat management determine output and beam shape. | Identify correct assemblies and verify aim, indicators and required visibility. |
| Seating, belts and restraints | Body-mounted / seat-integrated belt; adjustable / fixed seat | The belt load path and occupant range must be reviewed with anchors, track and floor. | Record fit, egress, anchor review and compatible donor restraints. |
| Pedals and controls | Mechanical / electronic accelerator; suspended / floor-mounted pedals | Travel, return, leverage, interference and command plausibility depend on layout. | Inspect positive return, clearances and full seat-adjustment range before motion testing. |

For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

Use the parts identity record and the service procedure for the exact donor. EPA's federal tampering and defeat-device provisions can apply to emissions-related hardware or software. Identify supporting compliance evidence for the exact configuration. In California, check the specific Executive Order and application where an exemption is relevant. For road use confirm state and local rules for registration, equipment, noise and inspection with the responsible authority. Colorado is the program's worked state example. references.title: Exterior, glazing, cabin and access · Hood to Door latch and striker
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Hood

**Function.** Closes engine compartment while allowing service access.

**Design.** Plan hinges, primary/secondary latches, load, sightline and edge clearance.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Form reviewed panel or align compatible donor hood and reinforcements.

**Verify.** Verify latch redundancy where required, clearance and service opening.

### Hood latch and secondary catch

**Function.** Retain hood under airflow and incidentally released primary latch.

**Design.** Match striker, catch reach and support stiffness.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit approved latches and guided release cable on reinforced mounts.

**Verify.** Perform specified pull, release and secondary retention checks.

### Fender and wheelhouse liner

**Function.** Cover wheel and manage spray, debris and airflow.

**Design.** Set coverage and clearance across full combined steer and wheel travel.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Template a liner or panel with serviceable clips and protected edges.

**Verify.** Check tire clearance at all intended travel combinations.

### Front fascia and grille

**Function.** Manage airflow, protect openings and house sensors.

**Design.** Define open area, mounts, lamp clearance and radar compatibility.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit shaped panel and approved sensor-compatible inserts.

**Verify.** Check cooling, retention, sensor function and edges.

### Bumper beam and crash absorbers

**Function.** Route impact loads through a designed crush sequence.

**Design.** Match vehicle structure and energy absorption design.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Retain engineered compatible beam and absorbers and prescribed fasteners.

**Verify.** Verify condition, alignment and documented structural compatibility.

### Door shell and intrusion beam

**Function.** Support closures and contribute to side impact protection.

**Design.** Plan hinge/latch reactions, regulator space, drainage and approved beam continuity.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit a compatible structural door or qualified reviewed design; form removable skins separately.

**Verify.** Check opening geometry, load paths and drain operation.

### Door hinge and pins

**Function.** Support and guide door travel.

**Design.** Match mass, pivot alignment, opening angle and reinforcement.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install matched hinge and locate shims to set gaps without the latch lifting the door.

**Verify.** Measure sag, gaps and full travel.

### Door latch and striker

**Function.** Retain door and release it on command.

**Design.** Match catch, striker orientation, handle cable and interlock.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit approved latch and adjust striker only after hinge and glass alignment.

**Verify.** Check full latch, inside/outside release and emergency exit.

references.title: Exterior, glazing, cabin and access · Door handle and lock actuator to Washer reservoir, hoses and jets
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Door handle and lock actuator

**Function.** Operate latch and central locking.

**Design.** Define rod or cable travel, electrical control and manual release.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Route controls away from moving glass and verify correct retaining clips.

**Verify.** Cycle each handle and lock from both sides.

### Window regulator

**Function.** Moves and locates door glass.

**Design.** Match guide paths, drive torque and anti-pinch controls where equipped.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit matched cable/scissor regulator and set glass stops per service data.

**Verify.** Check the full sweep, sealing and prescribed anti-pinch initialization.

### Door weatherstrip and vapor barrier

**Function.** Limit wind and water transfer to cabin.

**Design.** Choose compression profile, adhesive and unblocked drain path.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit seal to a clean flange and reseal inner barrier around harness exits.

**Verify.** Run a controlled water test and inspect inside trim and sill.

### Windshield

**Function.** Provides forward view and can have a structural or optical role.

**Design.** Match rated laminated glazing, optical area, camera bracket and adhesive system.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use qualified glazing installation and required safe drive-away cure time.

**Verify.** Verify bond, leaks and associated ADAS calibration.

### Side and rear glass

**Function.** Provide visibility and close openings.

**Design.** Specify approved glazing type, curvature, encapsulation and defrost provisions.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install the position-specific glass into correct guides or bonded aperture.

**Verify.** Check markings, movement, sealing and electrical function.

### Wiper arms and blades

**Function.** Sweep water from specified viewing areas.

**Design.** Match length, park angle, downforce and collision-free sweep.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit correctly indexed arms and approved blades.

**Verify.** Check on wet glass at all speeds and verify park position.

### Wiper linkage

**Function.** Converts motor rotation to coordinated blade motion.

**Design.** Choose crank radius, pivot positions and protected sweep limits.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install matched linkages in the motor park position.

**Verify.** Check link clearance, backlash and both blade endpoints.

### Washer reservoir, hoses and jets

**Function.** Store and deliver cleaning fluid to the glass.

**Design.** Size volume; match fluid, routing and nozzle coverage.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Mount tank securely, route hoses clear of hinges and aim nozzles.

**Verify.** Check for leaks and wet coverage across the working wipe area.

references.title: How to account for every installed part
references.body:
# Build-specific parts reconciliation

The teaching atlas lists common light-vehicle parts and service assemblies across multiple architectures. A gasoline manual, a diesel automatic and a battery-electric car have different inventories. The as-built bill of materials establishes what **your particular car** contains, down to separately installed hardware. Start with the actual model year, market, engine, transmission, option codes and donor/source identity. Mark privacy-sensitive paperwork for private instructor review.

1. Make a system tree for the exact vehicle. Give each parent assembly an ID. Identify the source of every child from a dated OEM parts catalog or exploded figure, engineering drawing, kit packing list, supplier specification, harness diagram or direct teardown. A commercial catalog is good for identity and fitment. Use separate authoritative service data for torque, installation and test limits. For original parts, assign drawing numbers and revisions yourself.
2. Start a line in As-Built-BOM.csv for each **part at each installation position**, including each clip, washer, spacer, seal, terminal, retainer, ground strap, hose end, fluid charge, service label and replacement-only fastener. Split left/right, front/rear, orientation and hardware stack order; link each to its parent. A separate serialized component gets its own instance. Account for consumables retained on the finished part, e.g. coating or sealant by product, batch and measured or specified amount where applicable. Mark discarded assembly aids separately.
3. Tie every row to an approved configuration. Record exact part/revision, the number or amount required, received or made, installed and independently verified, with units. Compare numbers at that installation position; purchased spare stock belongs to inventory, not installed quantity. Add any part missing from the teaching atlas. Mark a nonapplicable teaching family with the architecture-specific reason. A missing source entry is an open item.
4. Distinguish **make** (original or drawing-controlled part), **assemble** (purchased parts you personally integrated), **buy** (approved component) and **specialist** (named service or operation). Record material, tooling, process, measured features or supplier documents and who inspected it. Document critical work before it is hidden. Preserve service access and replace-only rules.
5. For a sealed bought assembly with no serviceable internal list, identify its make, model, revision or serial where available, supplier and functional boundary. List every separately fitted connector, seal, mount and fastener. If the manufacturer publishes a serviceable breakdown or you rebuild it, expand the children you actually service. Leave inaccessible internal details marked as supplier-controlled. Do not dismantle restraint inflators or sealed traction assemblies for an inventory exercise.
6. Reconcile from both directions. Walk each drawing callout into the build ledger, then walk each real installed item back to a drawing, receipt, material record or revision. Have a second person inspect quantities, location, retention and test evidence. Mark each row accepted, absent by design, awaiting evidence, rework or spare. Release a function only when all its relevant rows and measured acceptance tests have passed. Record who accepted the change. The complete car still requires the existing witnessed commissioning demonstration and its intended-use approvals.

## Worked example

The SP-01 removable-plate fixture drawing calls for one plate and one fastener/washer stack at each of two identified positions. Its practice board supplies tapped holes. The separate example CSV includes eight rows. They identify the board, the plate, two labeled mounting positions as parent groups, and the two screws and two washers distributed under those groups. Parent groups carry no physical quantities. A missing right washer is an intentional open finding. Correct the installed count only after fitting the washer; update verified count only after reinspection. Accepting the measured board and plate as individual parts leaves fixture release on hold until the corrected right stack is verified. An unused spare remains a stock item.

## Graduation review

Turn in the assembly tree, marked exploded views, drawing revisions, actual bill of materials, inspection evidence, change records and final service schedule. Account for every called-out or observed item and every receiving/installation discrepancy. An instructor must be able to pick an item on the physical car, identify who made or fitted it, locate its source or released drawing, and see how it passed the appropriate acceptance check. A passing written exam cannot certify workmanship, registration, emissions compliance or crashworthiness.

writing.prompt: Use full-size seat and glazing references. Submit a section drawing, buck stations, attachment detail, target gaps and an access test. Identify required lighting or glazing evidence and link the selected finish process to its safety data and shop controls. Include a labeled drawing or table in the work record and identify the applicable shop or legal requirement.

writing.title: Component selection and evidence
writing.prompt: For this course examine Body panel and surface finish; Closures, hinges, latch and seals; Glazing, wiper and washer; Lighting and signaling; Seating, belts and restraints; Pedals and controls. Identify each applicable family on your own vehicle or donor and explain absent families. Use two identified alternatives for at least one consequential choice. Show the job each design performs, how its operating principle differs, one failure mode and a test that separates the alternatives. Identify a real model or part number for each shortlisted candidate. Compare a sourced limit or performance figure under common conditions, interfaces, legal or shop implications and service access. Defend your choice and explain one change that would reverse it. Link your drawing and physical observation or measurement to the build record.

writing.title: Workshop record · Size a removable speaker adapter without fouling the glass
writing.prompt: Make a card or sheet adapter using actual driver and opening templates. Measure the least clearance throughout glass travel, preserve water management and document all fasteners. List your donor or drawing revision, part identities, position, material or rating, method, who made or fitted each item, and the governing source. State the goal, the baseline test, a controlled change, a potential adverse effect, comparable measured results, acceptance threshold and rollback. Include an attributable photograph, recorded direct observation or measurement. An inert prototype or mock-up qualifies for this comparison exercise when the vehicle modification requires specialist or legal approval. Identify exactly which vehicle results are still unproven.
